entries.summary: The Iloilo River Esplanade is a linear public park following both banks of the Iloilo River. Its river-edge paths connect several city districts, offering a view of Iloilo shaped by water rather than its downtown streets.
overview: The Iloilo River Esplanade is an urban promenade and linear park along the Iloilo River in Iloilo City. Its developed sections extend on both banks, between the Carpenter Bridge area in Mandurriao and Molo and the Drilon Bridge area toward City Proper and Lapuz. The project forms part of the rehabilitation of the river and was designed by landscape architect Paulo Alcazaren.

Its appeal is the relationship between the river and the city: a visitor can focus on a particular river-edge section rather than treating the entire esplanade as one short stop. A place pin or an estimated visit duration does not describe the distance of a complete end-to-end walk. Choose the section you intend to visit before arranging a pickup.

entries.summary: Casa Real de Iloilo is the old provincial capitol, associated with Iloilo’s Spanish-period administration and later civic government. It is a historic government building in Iloilo City, separate from the modern capitol and nearby museums.
overview: Casa Real de Iloilo, also called the Old Iloilo Provincial Capitol, served as the provincial government’s seat from the Spanish colonial period until 2006. The building was associated with the residence and offices of senior colonial officials and later with the civic administration of Iloilo.

Its significance is institutional as well as architectural: it helps explain where provincial authority was based before the newer government complex. A visitor should distinguish the old capitol from the modern capitol building and the museums in the surrounding area. The historical identity does not establish that every interior room is open to visitors on an ordinary day.

entries.summary: Taytay Boni, also called Puente de Boni, is an 1854 stone bridge in Miagao, Iloilo. Built for horse-drawn carriages, its yellow-coral-stone construction and prominent finial-topped posts make it a distinctive heritage stop.

The municipal history account describes large newel posts topped with pyramid-shaped finials, features that help explain the structure’s distinctive appearance. This is a particular bridge heritage site in Miagao, separate from a visit inside the parish church. Current access around the structure should be checked locally.
